title: Weekly POC Sync — heuristic tuning and emergency routes
summary: Reviewed week-over-week POC metrics (latency / failure modes), discussed heuristic tuning for token cutoff and KV cache behavior, compared two catalog candidates for version pinning, and agreed emergency fallback routes and owners. Agreed next steps: run 24h degraded-path soak, share quantization benchmark sheet, and update runbook for cutover criteria.
action_items: Owner: Jonah Li; Item: Run 24-hour degraded-path soak with v1.3a pinned and capture p99 latency + token-cost; Due: 2026-01-23
Owner: Sarah Nguyen; Item: Provide 3 representative prompt sets (support/clinical-summary, intake-parsing, guidance-gen) for regression checks; Due: 2026-01-22
Owner: Carlos Herrera; Item: Confirm network egress rules for VPC peering and share firewall policy snippet; Due: 2026-01-21
Owner: Maya Patel; Item: Share quantization benchmark spreadsheet and recommended quant profiles for BrightHealth workload; Due: 2026-01-22
next_steps: Start 24h soak on staging-routing -> runbook to observe soft-fallback triggers
SE to upload latency/cost CSV to shared drive and tag product for review
Schedule cutover tabletop drill next Wed (2026-01-28) to rehearse emergency route activation
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Sarah, Carlos, Priya (BrightHealth)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): quick sync on metrics, some noisy words on KV cash behavior, action items listed below.

[00:00] Maya: okay team, thanks for joining. quick agenda — rerun the soak results, pick an anchor model for pinning, and lock down emergency routes. anyone need to add?
[00:12] Sarah: no, that's good. i mostly want to know whether the p99 latency bump last night is model-related or infra. we saw a spike around 02:40 PST.
[00:22] Jonah: yeah i dug into that — preliminary appears to be interplay between long-prefix sessions and the KV cache warmup. KV cache logs show a bunch of misses during sequence 1-3, then stabilizes. sometimes transcript has "KV cash" which is funny.
[00:34] Carlos: to add, the autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough because our bursting policy is conservative; we saw queueing.
[00:43] Maya: right, so two levers: infra (autoscale) and model profile (quantization / shorter context heuristics). today let's compare the two catalog candidates: v1.2-q4 (light quant) vs v1.3a (newer decoder, slightly higher token cost but better coherency).
[01:05] Priya: for product, coherence on the clinical-summary prompts is higher priority than raw cost. a hallucination on a discharge summary is worse than 20% extra token cost.
[01:18] Sarah: agreed. but we still need to hit 200ms median and keep p99 under 700ms if possible. what were we seeing in the soak?
[01:29] Jonah: soak numbers — median tokens/time was 180ms, p95 around 420, p99 spiked to 820 during that KV-miss window. with v1.3a pinned we see slightly better conditional coherence but p99 still hits 700-900 in cold-start tails. v1.2-q4 had p99 lower by ~80ms but produced shorter, sometimes choppier completions.
[01:58] Maya: so tradeoff is cost/latency vs quality. our recommendation previously was to pin v1.3a on staging and use soft fallback to v1.2-q4 if latency exceeds threshold for X minutes.
[02:12] Sarah: what's the exact trigger we should simulate? we want an automated escape hatch before customers observe failures.
[02:20] Jonah: proposal: if rolling p99 > 800ms for 5 minutes AND error rate > 0.5%, route new sessions to v1.2-q4 for 10 minutes, then evaluate. also make the alert noisy but human-confirm gating for production cutovers.
[02:37] Carlos: can that routing be regional? we saw tail latency concentrated in us-west-2 due to that maintenance window.
[02:45] Maya: yes, routing supports region policies; we can set the soft fallback regionally and also have a global emergency route.
[02:52] Sarah: curious about the KV cache warmup — can we do prefix caching at request-time to avoid the tail?
[03:01] Jonah: we have prefix caching, but the issue is the prompt distribution: many of your prompts begin with long clinical templates, so balance of cache hit/miss gets weird. we can prewarm popular prefixes based on logs but that adds more maintenance.
[03:16] Priya: hmm, could be a good middle ground — prewarm top 50 prefixes from last week for the soak and see how p99 moves.
[03:24] Jonah: yeah i'll script that for the soak.
[03:28] Maya: let's talk about quantization profiles — jonah, you had suggested two profiles: q4-lite and q8-mixed?
[03:35] Jonah: correct. q4-lite reduces memory and token cost but sometimes truncates semantic depth; q8-mixed keeps better quality at slightly higher cost. brighthealth's clinical needs likely need q8 on the decoders. we recommended v1.3a with q8 for production, but for emergency fallback we keep v1.2-q4.
[03:56] Sarah: ok. can you attach the benchmark spreadsheet after the call? we'll run it through our QA prompts.
[04:03] Maya: yes i'll share.
[04:07] Carlos: one security note — we need to confirm KMS integration for key rotation and that audit logs capture model selection events. compliance wants model pin changes in the audit trail.
[04:18] Jonah: audit logs include routing decisions and model IDs, but i'll double-check the retention window and whether the private deployment agent pushes those logs to your SIEM. sometimes the transcription calls it "model id 1.3 a" and the export mangles it.
[04:32] Sarah: also SSO team asked about RBAC for the Redwood console — we need to make sure product folks can't accidentally flip pin policies.
[04:40] Maya: yep, RBAC demo in next week's call? we can schedule a short walkthrough.
[04:46] Priya: that'd help.
[04:49] Maya: quick review of the soak plan — jonah runs 24-hour degraded-path soak on staging with prewarmed prefixes, v1.3a pinned, soft fallback to v1.2-q4, and collects pXX + token-cost. sarah provides prompts; carlos confirms network egress.
[05:05] Sarah: i'll drop prompt sets into the shared folder by tomorrow.
[05:10] Carlos: firewall snippet by EOD.
[05:13] Jonah: starting soak tonight at 20:00 UTC and will push results by 2026-01-23 morning.
[05:18] Maya: great. next, cutover tabletop — do we want people on-call for that drill?
[05:23] Priya: yes, product, infra, and dev defenders should be on the tabletop. we'll confirm attendees.
[05:29] Maya: any objections to the rollback runbook language? i proposed an explicit 3-step: route, monitor 5min, then if no improvement rollback and notify.
[05:37] Sarah: sounds reasonable but add an approval step for production only — a human confirm within 10 minutes unless the error rate passes an emergency threshold.
[05:46] Jonah: noted, i'll update.
[05:49] [longer section of technical clarifying Q&A: 05:49-18:20 — summarized below]
[18:21] Jonah: technical clarifications: the runtime's kernel switch is mostly invisible, but quantized kernels can change tail latency distribution. also our continuous batching config can be tuned to pause at X ms to reduce p99 noise.
[18:40] Carlos: how invasive is the kernel change? does it require model recompilation?
[18:44] Jonah: minor recompile on the serving side; we can ship it as a compatible variant — no model retrain. the model id just points to a compiled artifact.
[18:53] Sarah: and about audit logs, can redwood push model-change events to our webhook?
[18:58] Maya: yes, we support webhook forwarding for audit events; jonah will confirm event taxa and sample payloads.
[19:07] Priya: any notes on pricing when fallback triggers? we need to budget for possible 10% cost increase during emergencies.
[19:13] Maya: we'll add an estimated worst-case in the shared cost model sheet.
[19:18] Sarah: also curious whether regional cutover reduces cost exposure — maybe route only affected region to fallback.
[19:25] Jonah: regional fallback is simplest and recommended.
[19:29] Maya: ok, to wrap — recap of owners and dates (see action items). does anyone have open blockers?
[19:38] Carlos: nothing other than the firewall snippet and egress confirmation.
[19:42] Sarah: no blockers.
[19:44] Priya: none.
[19:45] Maya: thanks all. we'll send summary and calendar invite for the tabletop drill next Wed.
[19:50] End of transcript.
